Puerto del Rosario|Spain.f: Puerto del Rosario was called Puerto de Cabras, the Port of the Goats, until it was renamed in 1957.

Rhodes|Greece.f: The Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders, was finished in 280 BC and toppled by an earthquake in 226 BC.

Evenes|Norway.f: A mobile hospital was built inside a small mountain at Osmarka, near Evenes airport, using NATO infrastructure funds.

Bodø|Norway.f: Saltstraumen, near Bodo, has one of the strongest tidal currents in the world, with water speeds reaching 22 knots.

Mahón|Spain.f: Mahon's natural harbour is 5 km long, among the longest in the world, and mayonnaise is thought to have originated here.

Kittilä|Finland.f: Finland's lowest recorded temperature, -51.5 C, was measured at Pokka in Kittila in January 1999.

Ivalo|Finland.f: Retreating German troops severely damaged Ivalo during the Lapland War of 1944 to 1945, and the village was rebuilt afterwards.

Kos|Greece.f: Hippocrates is thought to have been born on Kos, and a plane tree in Kos town is traditionally linked to where he taught.

Corfu|Greece.f: Corfu and its mother city Corinth fought what Thucydides records as the first naval battle in Greek history, in 665 BC.

Visby|Sweden.f: Visby's medieval ring wall is 3.4 km long and still largely intact, and the town has been a UNESCO site since 1995.

Terceira|Portugal.f: Terceira is home to Angra do Heroismo, the oldest city in the Azores and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Santa Maria (Azores)|Portugal.f: Santa Maria was the first Azores island to be colonized and is the southernmost island of the archipelago.

Porto Santo|Portugal.f: Rabbits released by Porto Santo's first captain multiplied catastrophically and devastated the island's native flora.

Lakselv|Norway.f: Lakselv means Salmon River in Norwegian, and the river through the village is popular for summer salmon fishing.

Usinsk|Russia.f: Usinsk was founded in 1966 at newly found oil deposits, and three quarters of Komi's oil now comes from fields around it.

Andenes|Norway.f: Andenes sits beside a narrow stretch of continental shelf, which made it a major centre for whale watching.

Bardufoss|Norway.f: Bardufoss airport was renamed Snowman International in 2011 after a commercial flight from Manchester landed for the celebrations.

Kefalonia|Greece.f: A 1953 earthquake destroyed almost all the settlements on Kefalonia, leaving only Fiskardo in the north untouched.

Mytilene|Greece.f: In 428 BC Athens voted to massacre all of Mytilene's men, then reversed itself next day and sent a fast trireme to cancel it.

Karpathos|Greece.f: Karpathos is the mythological homeland of the Titan Iapetus and the birthplace of the sea god Proteus.

Zakynthos|Greece.f: Ancient Athens prized Zakynthos for ship tar, dredged from Lake Keri on myrtle branches tied to the ends of poles.

Santa Cruz de La Palma|Spain.f: Santa Cruz de La Palma is said to have had the first democratically elected town hall in Spain.

Alta|Norway.f: The rock carvings at Alta, made between about 7000 BC and 500 BC, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Samos|Greece.f: Samos was home to Aristarchus, the astronomer credited with the first recorded heliocentric model of the Solar System.

Enontekio|Finland.f: Enontekio's Kasivarsi, the Arm, got its name because pre-war Finland's borders formed a woman's figure with this area as her raised arm.

Kuressaare|Estonia.f: Kuressaare was officially renamed Kingissepa from 1952 to 1988, after a Bolshevik who was born there.

Sønderborg|Denmark.f: In the 1920 plebiscite, 56.2% of Sonderborg's voters chose to stay in Germany, though Northern Schleswig returned to Denmark.

Brač|Croatia.f: Brac's white limestone was used to build Diocletian's Palace in Split and the Canadian National Vimy Memorial.

Pico|Portugal.f: Ponta do Pico on Pico Island is the highest mountain in Portugal and the highest point of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

Gällivare|Sweden.f: Max Hamburgers, Sweden's second-largest fast food chain, was founded in Gallivare.

Pantelleria|Italy.f: The Arabs called Pantelleria Bint al-Riyah, Daughter of the Winds, after the strong gales off the North African coast.

Skiathos|Greece.f: Skiathos has over 60 mostly sandy beaches along only 44 km of coastline.

Horta|Portugal.f: Horta's marina walls and walkways are covered with paintings left by transatlantic yacht crews, noting their boats and the year.

Kärdla|Estonia.f: A 455 million year old meteorite crater lies just southeast of Kardla on the island of Hiiumaa.

Chios|Greece.f: Chios is the Mastic Island, and seven villages in its south have controlled mastic gum production since Roman times.

Höfn|Iceland.f: Hofn holds a lobster festival, Humarhatid, every year on the first weekend of July.

Velas|Portugal.f: A volcanic eruption in 1580 on Sao Jorge near Velas lasted four months and dropped ash as far away as Terceira.

Sandnessjøen|Norway.f: Sandnessjoen had special trading privileges from the late 1600s but only received official town status in 1999.

Ísafjörður|Iceland.f: Isafjordur's old Danish trading quarter has the oldest collection of timber frame houses in Iceland, some from the 1750s.

Santa Cruz da Graciosa|Portugal.f: Graciosa joined the global nuclear test ban treaty verification network in 2010 with a monitoring station on the island.
